candidates.title: Operando IR/EPR donor-adduct screen
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA versus TEOA causes different donor-associated cobalt or substrate-bound species under matched P01 conditions, while bounding what any spectral differences can and cannot establish about the CO/H2 shift.
candidates.source_to_proposal: GX011 suggests TEOA can form catalyst adduct-like species in a bipyridine carbonyl system, motivating a cautious transfer test for donor-specific adduct chemistry in Co-bpy rather than assuming the same species. EV016 shows EPR can detect TEOA-derived radicals and that TEA/TEOA can differ in line shape because of physical properties, supporting donor-comparative EPR with matched blanks. EV068 supports operando FTIR/EPR to follow working-state interactions instead of recovered samples only. EV085 warns that donor decomposition and decomposition-derived active species can confound assignments, so donor-free and no-cobalt controls are required and any signal must be treated as descriptive unless tied to matched catalytic outputs.

comparisons.inference: Primary donor-identity comparison. Reproducible donor-specific IR bands or EPR features under otherwise matched conditions would support a cobalt-speciation or donor-adduct contribution, but not by itself prove causality for CO/H2.

Tests whether TEOA-dependent features require the donor. Features absent without donor are consistent with donor-derived radicals, donor binding, or donor-enabled substrate intermediates, but remain assignment-limited.
Tests whether candidate features require cobalt. Signals present in both groups are background from donor, support, solvent, or CO2 handling rather than cobalt-specific species.

Tests whether candidate TEOA-associated features are light-generated. A light-only appearance supports turnover-related or photogenerated species; persistence in dark suggests pre-equilibrium binding or background chemistry.

procedure: Prepare matched baseline-family mixtures using the verified P01 component identities; keep vessel geometry, gas handling, solvent ratio, and sampling timing identical across groups.

Run a short pilot to choose concentration and optical path windows that avoid detector saturation and give measurable cobalt-region EPR/IR baselines; lock those settings before the TEA versus TEOA comparison.
Collect dark/background spectra first, then acquire operando or rapid sealed near-operando IR and EPR data under CO2 during illumination for each group using the same time points.

Pair the spectral campaign with matched product analysis from the same batches or parallel identically prepared batches so spectral differences can be compared with CO and H2 outputs without assuming causation.
Use replicate preparations and conservative peak assignment rules, reporting unmatched or ambiguous features as unknown signals rather than named intermediates.
measurements: In situ or near-operando IR difference spectra under CO2 and illumination, tracking donor-dependent new bands, band shifts, and growth/decay behavior relative to dark and donor-free baselines.
In situ or rapid-freeze/rapid-transfer EPR spectra, tracking appearance, disappearance, g-pattern changes, and line broadening under TEA versus TEOA conditions.
Matched catalytic readouts from parallel or same-batch experiments: CO and H2 amounts or rates, reported together rather than selectivity alone.
Background spectra from donor-free, no-cobalt, and dark controls to establish which signals are not cobalt-specific or not light-dependent.
If signal strength allows, time ordering of spectral changes relative to product formation; this can show correlation but cannot by itself identify the sole active species.
candidates.supports: H04 is supported if, under the locked matched P01 comparison, TEA and TEOA show reproducibly different cobalt-requiring and light-dependent IR and/or EPR signatures, or different persistence/loss of such signatures over time, and those differences track a donor-dependent CO/H2 change better than donor-free or no-cobalt backgrounds do.
candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in cobalt-requiring, light-dependent IR/EPR observables within detection limits while catalytic CO/H2 still differs under the same matched conditions, favoring explanations upstream in donor photochemistry or downstream in proton/CO2 handling rather than cobalt-state divergence.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if spectra are too weak, dominated by background/support signals, changed by viscosity or other physical effects without cobalt specificity, or if donor-dependent signals appear but cannot be distinguished from donor decomposition, generic radical formation, or unsupported assignments. Correlation without clean controls also remains inconclusive.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-backed P01 formulation family only for component identity, not exact invented numbers. First verify the baseline recipe from source records. Then run pilots to set sample concentration, path length, irradiation interval, and EPR acquisition mode by the rule that cobalt-containing samples must show stable unsaturated baselines and donor-free/no-cobalt controls must remain interpretable. If TEA and TEOA differ strongly in viscosity or optical density, adjust only the measurement configuration, not the chemical formulation, and document that this preserves matched chemistry while changing detection settings. Choose time points by a calibration run that captures pre-illumination, early illumination, and a later turnover window without exhausting the sample.
candidates.limitations: Assignments are transferred from nonidentical systems and may not map to Co-bpy. IR/EPR can reveal donor-dependent species or state changes but cannot alone establish the full catalytic mechanism, the exact structure of the active cobalt species, or product origin. TEA/TEOA physical-property differences can alter line shape and transport, so apparent spectral differences are not automatically chemical. Near-operando aliquots may miss the true instantaneous working state. No-cobalt control uses a different total composition and is a background screen, not a full single-factor catalytic comparison.

candidates.title: P02 donor-substitution bridge for cobalt-state and quenching readouts
candidates.purpose: Test in the supplementary homogeneous cobalt platform whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes cobalt-state-sensitive observables or donor-coupled quenching behavior under otherwise matched conditions, then compare only the qualitative direction of donor effects to the primary P01 system.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV065 supports a defined homogeneous cobalt photocatalytic platform with TEOA and measurable quenching; EV053 supports using fluorescence/UV-vis to distinguish donor-versus-catalyst quenching routes; EV052 and GX008 support operando or near-operando state tracking plus negative controls. Proposed transfer is limited: this is a cleaner bridge assay, not the target Co-bpy/g-C3N4 chemistry, so agreement would support donor-linked state trends while disagreement could reflect platform-specific speciation.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-variable test for donor-linked differences in cobalt-state-sensitive spectra, quenching behavior, and catalytic output within P02.
Separates cobalt-dependent signatures from TEOA/photosensitizer background; not a single-factor causal test because sample purpose also changes.
Separates cobalt-dependent signatures from TEA/photosensitizer background; not a single-factor causal test because sample purpose also changes.
Checks whether donor substitution alone changes background quenching or spectral baselines, bounding interpretation of the full-mixture contrast.

procedure: Prepare matched P02 mixtures and donor-specific blanks with verified identical cobalt catalyst, photosensitizer, solvent family, gas handling, optical path, and illumination settings except for donor identity or cobalt omission as assigned.

Run a pilot to set concentrations, path length, and acquisition timing within linear absorbance/emission response and without detector saturation; if donor or catalyst causes severe inner-filter or turbidity artifacts, dilute all groups proportionally and repeat matched measurements.

Collect donor-sensitive quenching data and cobalt-state-sensitive spectra before illumination and during a short matched illumination window, using donor-specific blanks and dark references to aid assignment.

In the same matched reaction sets, quantify CO and H2 together after the chosen illumination interval so spectroscopic directionality can be compared with catalytic output without claiming mechanistic proof.
measurements: Steady-state or time-resolved photosensitizer emission quenching versus donor and cobalt presence; this shows relative quenching behavior but cannot by itself identify the full catalytic pathway.

UV-vis spectral changes of the cobalt-containing mixture before and during illumination; these can indicate donor-linked state changes or aggregation but cannot uniquely assign a specific cobalt intermediate without independent confirmation.

If available, operando or near-operando Co K-edge XAS/XANES/EXAFS on matched TEA and TEOA mixtures; these can report average oxidation-state and coordination-environment changes but may miss minority active species.
GC quantification of CO and H2 from the same matched runs; this establishes product distribution changes but not their sole cause.
candidates.supports: Support for H04 would be a reproducible donor-dependent change between E23G01 and E23G02 in cobalt-associated spectral or operando XAS observables that is absent or much smaller in the corresponding cobalt-free blanks, with the qualitative donor trend aligning with a donor-linked change in CO/H2 output. Agreement in direction with analogous P01 observations would strengthen transfer, while remaining bounded to trend-level rather than identity-level claims.
candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if E23G01 and E23G02 show indistinguishable cobalt-dependent spectra and quenching-corrected state readouts across the operando window, while catalytic differences persist or are explained by donor-only blank behavior. It is also weakened if apparent donor differences arise mainly in E23G03 versus E23G04, indicating upstream donor/photosensitizer effects without clear cobalt-state divergence.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if donor substitution changes optical baselines, viscosity, solubility, or inner-filter behavior enough to prevent matched interpretation; if cobalt signals are below detection or dominated by broad unresolved features; if TEA and TEOA require materially different concentration windows to keep the assay stable; or if P02 shows donor effects but P01 comparison data are unavailable for bridging.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-defined P02 component identities and solvent family, but verify exact concentrations and illumination settings from the supplied source before execution. If any setting is still uncertain, choose it by pilot rules: maintain measurable CO/H2 within a short assay window, keep absorbance/emission in the instrument linear range, keep cobalt and photosensitizer solutions visibly homogeneous, and use one common setting for both donors whenever possible. If one donor destabilizes the mixture under the common setting, reduce all concentrations proportionally and re-run the full matched set rather than optimizing donors separately.
candidates.limitations: Catalyst architecture differs from the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 target, so this is a transfer test rather than a direct explanation of P01. Donor substitution can change medium properties and quenching simultaneously, and homogeneous average-state methods may not reveal minority active species. Cobalt-free blanks help bound but do not eliminate confounding. Spectral changes alone cannot establish exact coordination structures or prove causality for product selectivity.

candidates.title: Ligand and support omission around donor effect
candidates.purpose: Test whether a TEA-versus-TEOA cobalt-state difference requires the full Co-bpy/g-C3N4 assembly or is already present when bpy or g-C3N4 is omitted one factor at a time, while also checking whether any CO/H2 signal remains attributable to background pathways.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the primary CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4+TEOA formulation family and thus justifies omitting bpy or g-C3N4 relative to that baseline. GX008 supports negative-control logic and paired characterization/product analysis rather than relying on catalytic output alone. EV081 shows that no-catalyst or partial-system backgrounds can still yield CO and H2, so omission results must be interpreted as necessity tests, not proof of mechanism. GX016 supports the broader idea that cobalt-centered identity matters to product selectivity under TEOA photocatalysis, motivating tests of whether donor-linked effects disappear when cobalt coordination context is simplified. The proposed transfer is a controlled omission study in the P01-style system; it does not assume literature-established active-species identity or fully matched chemistry beyond the named components.

groups.description: Support-omission formulation with TEOA and TEA run as separate matched subruns under the same card workflow

factors.name: donor
factors.value: TEOA or TEA in separate matched subruns

comparisons.inference: Primary donor-substitution benchmark in the full assembly. A reproducible difference in cobalt-state observables or stability trend here is necessary before omission data can localize where divergence emerges.

Tests whether donor-dependent cobalt-state divergence persists without bpy. Persistence would indicate that a full Co-bpy assembly is not required for the observed donor effect; disappearance would suggest dependence on ligand-defined coordination context.

Omission test for ligand necessity under TEOA. Any loss or major alteration of cobalt-state signatures or catalytic output indicates dependence on bpy, but this does not isolate a donor effect because donor is fixed.

Descriptive comparison only if E24G05 is implemented first with TEOA, then repeated with TEA as matched subruns. Because support omission and donor handling are not simultaneously encoded as separate groups here, support-related conclusions must be bounded and human review should check subrun comparability before causal interpretation.

procedure: Verify the P01 baseline composition from the supplied source, then prepare matched reaction mixtures that differ only by the planned omission or donor identity and include fresh blanks/background references for spectroscopy and gas analysis.

Run a short pilot to set sample concentration, optical density, and acquisition timing so cobalt-state signals are detectable without detector saturation; keep the same calibrated window for all groups within each analytical session.
For each group, record pre-illumination and near-operando cobalt-state observables under CO2 and matched illumination, then collect paired gas-product data from the same workflow.

Compare donor effects first within the full assembly and within the ligand-omission pair; if support omission is pursued, run TEOA and TEA support-free subruns under the same calibrated workflow and treat them as bounded descriptive validation.
Interpret omissions as necessity tests and donor swaps as specificity tests; do not infer a single active species from one signature or from recovered samples alone.
measurements: Gas-phase CO and H2 quantified together by the same GC workflow for all groups; report amount and CO/H2 distribution, noting that product ratios alone cannot identify cobalt speciation.

Near-operando cobalt-state observable from an element- or coordination-sensitive method feasible in the lab context, such as XAS/XPS-compatible sampling or solution/solid UV-Vis features; state explicitly which sample state is measured and that assignments may remain ambiguous.

Pre- versus during-illumination change in cobalt-related spectral features or signal loss as a bounded stability/deactivation indicator; this can show donor- or omission-dependent change but cannot by itself prove the catalytically active state.
Background product formation in omission groups, used to bound non-full-assembly contributions; detection of CO or H2 here does not establish catalytic equivalence to the full system.
candidates.supports: H04 is supported if the full assembly shows a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in cobalt-state or stability observables, and the difference changes systematically when bpy is omitted or when support-free subruns are examined, indicating that donor-dependent divergence depends on ligand or support context rather than arising solely from generic donor chemistry. Stronger support occurs if the direction of the state/stability difference tracks the direction of CO/H2 changes across the matched groups.
candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give indistinguishable cobalt-state and stability observables in the full assembly within method resolution, and omission of bpy or g-C3N4 changes overall activity but does not reveal any donor-dependent cobalt-state divergence. It is further weakened if donor substitution affects CO/H2 while cobalt-state observables remain unchanged across all matched formulations.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if product signals are near background, cobalt-state signals are below detection or assignment is non-unique, omission groups cause severe optical or compositional changes that prevent comparable measurements, or support-free subruns are not adequately matched. A donor effect seen only in one method without corroboration or with drifting baselines should remain provisional.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations or illumination settings. Use the source-anchored P01 baseline after verification, then perform a pilot to choose the lowest concentration and path length that still provide stable cobalt-state signal above blank/background and measurable CO/H2 above analytical detection. Calibrate sampling time to a pre-conversion window where signals are detectable but bulk depletion is limited. If support-free mixtures change turbidity or absorbance, recalibrate acquisition settings using blanks while preserving identical reactor geometry, gas handling, and analytical timing across compared groups.
candidates.limitations: Direct TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head evidence in the exact P01 recipe is incomplete, so this card begins from a source-anchored but still pilot-verified baseline. Omission of bpy or g-C3N4 may create chemically different cobalt species rather than simple partial versions of the full catalyst, so omissions test dependence, not mechanistic continuity. Multi-factor support-free comparison is partially confounded unless implemented as explicit matched subruns. Recovered-sample measurements may miss the operating state, and generic spectral changes cannot by themselves establish the active species or exact coordination geometry.
